findings.topic: Optional goods pickup during Ship/Wagon movement
findings.source: authoritative-source.txt lines264–270; matching-rulebook.pdf printed p18; pdf-index-7-printed-page-18.png
findings.source_rule: After moving along a Waterway, a player may take an available Goods Tile; Wagon uses the same procedure along a Road.
findings.gap: Q11 directly asks movement, the number that can be taken when two goods lie on the connection, and travel on an empty connection. An answer saying one good correctly answers its quantity clause without resolving whether taking a good is compulsory. Its key says may take one, but the unrequested permission to refuse pickup should not silently be mandatory coverage.
findings.consequence: A player may complete the movement while deliberately leaving the available good on the connection. The movement does not depend on collecting a good.
findings.novelty: Explicit discretionary zero-pickup branch when a good is available, rather than a changed goods count, route, or named town. Analogous in coverage logic to testing one-of-two transfer permission separately from Town Hall capacity. No Tax interaction or other recombination is needed to establish the rule.
findings.adjudication_boundary: If Q11 is formally interpreted as requiring both the minimum and maximum legal pickup quantity, this proposal is redundant. Its wording does not clearly demand that interpretation; under the assigned rule against silently grading unrequested key facts, a narrow direct prompt is preferable.

proposed_questions.question: When a Ship or Wagon action crosses a connection with an available Goods Tile, must you take a good, or may you complete the move and leave it there?
proposed_questions.expected_answer: You may leave it there. Taking a good during Ship movement is optional, and Wagon follows the same procedure on Roads. You still move to the adjacent town.
source_references: Printed p18; authoritative-source.txt lines264–270; Ship says may take it, and Wagon is similar except Road instead of Waterway.
proposed_questions.novelty: Directly tests declining an available optional pickup. Q11 directly tests the one-good cap and empty-link travel, not compulsory versus optional pickup.
not_claimed_as_novelty: A Taxes calculation involving the uncollected good
